population.text: TL05 enrolled 78 subjects with EGFR mutations (57% of total enrollment N=137) with advanced NSCLC previously treated with applicable targeted therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy. For FDA's efficacy evaluation, 77 patients from TL05 receiving Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg Q3W were pooled with 37 patients from TL01 (total n=114); this 114-patient EGFR-mutated pooled population is a cross-trial pooled population, not TL05's own trial population.

citations.quote: The study enrolled 78 subjects with EGFR mutations, which was 57% of the total enrollment (N=137).

While the Applicant notes that the primary analysis of efficacy was based on the TL05 trial with supportive data from the TL01 trial, given the similarity in patient population between TL01 and TL05, the primary analysis population for FDA's evaluation of efficacy is the pooled population of patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC with disease progression following EGFR-directed therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy who received Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg Q3W in these two trials (77 patients from TL05 and 37 from TL01).

A total of 604 subjects with NSCLC were enrolled in the study, including 84 (approximately 14%) with EGFRm NSCLC (39 in the Dato-DXd arm and 45 in the docetaxel arm; Study TL01 PFS CSR body and Study TL01 EGFR Table 14.1.1.1).

result.text: The randomized-population PFS/OS analyses in the EGFR-mutated subgroup were post-hoc and evaluated as supportive evidence only. Post-hoc EGFR-mutated subgroup: ORR by BICR 41.0% (95% CI: 25.6, 57.9) vs 8.9% (95% CI: 2.5, 21.2) with docetaxel; PFS by BICR HR 0.39 (95% CI: 0.22, 0.69), median PFS 6.8 months (95% CI: 4.2, 8.2) vs 2.7 months (95% CI: 1.5, 4.4); OS HR 0.78 (95% CI: 0.45, 1.35) crossing 1 (non-significant), median OS 15.6 months (95% CI: 12.0, 16.9) vs 12.8 months (95% CI: 6.9, 17.2)

citations.quote: Analyses of PFS and OS from the randomized target patient population in TL01 were evaluated as supportive evidence only given the post-hoc nature of this subgroup analysis with a limited sample size.

In a post-hoc subgroup analysis in subjects with EGFRm NSCLC, Dato-DXd showed more than 4-fold increase in the rate of confirmed objective response assessed by BICR when compared to docetaxel (ORR with Dato-DXd was 41.0% [95% CI: 25.6, 57.9] versus 8.9% [95% CI: 2.5, 21.2] with docetaxel).

Clinically meaningful improvement in PFS by BICR with Dato-DXd compared to docetaxel was observed in adult subjects with locally advanced or metastatic EGFRm NSCLC who had received prior systemic therapy (HR: 0.39 [95% CI: 0.22, 0.69]; median PFS: 6.8 months [95% CI: 4.2, 8.2] with Dato-DXd versus 2.7 months [95% CI: 1.5, 4.4] with docetaxel; Applicant - Table 19).

In the primary analysis of OS, OS trended in favor of Dato-DXd (HR: 0.78 [95% CI: 0.45, 1.35]; median OS: 15.6 months [95% CI: 12.0, 16.9] with Dato-DXd versus 12.8 months [95% CI: 6.9, 17.2] with docetaxel; Applicant - Table 19).

target_moa.text: Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate; humanized IgG1 anti-Trop2 antibody linked to DXd, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a cleavable linker; upon binding Trop2 it internalizes and releases DXd causing DNA damage and apoptosis

citations.quote: Datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk (DATROWAY®, Dato-DXd) is a Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). The antibody is a humanized IgG1 directed against Trop2. The small molecule, DXd, is a topoisomerase I inhibitor attached to the antibody by a cleavable linker.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were stomatitis (71%), nausea (50%), alopecia (49%), fatigue (42%), constipation (31%), musculoskeletal pain (22%), rash (20%), and decreased appetite (20%); serious adverse reactions in 26%; significant risks are ILD/pneumonitis, ocular toxicity, and stomatitis

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge20%) were stomatitis (71%), nausea (50%), alopecia (49%), fatigue (42%), constipation (31%), musculoskeletal pain (22%), rash (20%), and decreased appetite (20%).
Among these 125 patients, serious adverse reactions occurred in 26% of patients; serious adverse reactions occurring in >1% of patients were COVID-19 (4%), stomatitis (2.4%), and pneumonia (1.6%).
Safety issues identified as significant and serious enough to warrant including in Warnings and Precautions section of labeling for Dato-DXd are, ILD/pneumonitis, ocular toxicity, and stomatitis.
